description: SPARS2 builds a sparse *spanner* like SPARS does: a small graph whose paths are nearly as short as the best paths. It keeps no dense graph, so it uses much less memory. SPARS2 tests each valid sample for *coverage* (no guard sees it within `Δ`), *connectivity* (it joins two components) and *interface* (it links two neighbouring guards); if all three fail, it samples near the sample to find where the regions of the guards meet, and it adds a shortcut when a path through a guard is more than `t` times too long. Construction stops after `M` samples in a row change nothing. With high probability, the paths then cost at most about `t` times the optimum plus a term in `Δ` (*asymptotic near-optimality*).

papers.title: Improving sparse roadmap spanners
papers.venue: 2013 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
